title: Acceptance scenario declaration
description: One acceptance scenario from section 8 of docs/sdd/01-specification.md, and what currently executes it. Constitution Article VII says acceptance scenarios are written before the code they accept, and asks of every change which scenario accepts it. A specification can carry forty-five of them while three are executed and nothing says so, because a scenario that is merely written looks exactly like a scenario that is met. These declarations are what make the difference visible: each scenario is either `referenced` by a named test or `not_executable` with the task that owes it.

id.description: The scenario identifier. Must appear as a `Scenario:` line in the specification.

title.description: The scenario's own title, copied from the specification so a renamed scenario shows up as a diff here rather than drifting silently.

state.description: 'referenced': a test names this scenario, so a reader can go from the scenario to the code that accepts it. 'not_executable': the components the scenario drives do not exist yet, and `owed_by` names the task that will build them. There is deliberately no third state: 'planned', 'partial' or 'covered elsewhere' would each be a way to stop counting a scenario without executing it.

referenced_by.description: Required on 'referenced': the tests that name this scenario, as `path::test_name`. Checked - each test must exist and its source must actually name the scenario, because a declaration that points at a test which never mentions it is the exact failure this registry exists to catch.

owed_by.description: Required on 'not_executable': the work-breakdown task that must exist before this scenario can be executed at all. A scenario owed by nobody is a scenario nobody will write.

note.description: Anything a reader needs that the fields above cannot carry - which half of a scenario is blocked, or which fixture covers the same ground from another angle.
